summary: This is a Docker Compose configuration file that defines a development container service. It sets up a single application service with specific build arguments, environment variables, port mappings, security settings, and volume mounts to create an isolated development environment with VS Code extensions persistence.

explanations.5: This tells Docker where to find the Dockerfile and related files needed to build the container image — in this case, in the .devcontainer folder.
explanations.7: These are variables passed into the Docker build process to customize how the image is constructed, like setting the Python version and user permissions.
explanations.8: APP_HOME is being set to /ap, which will be the main directory path inside the container where the application code lives.
explanations.14: Instead of running an application, this container will just execute 'sleep infinity', which keeps it running indefinitely so you can connect to it for development.
explanations.18: These are environment variables available inside the running container that match some of the build arguments — they're being set a second time to ensure they're available at runtime.
explanations.24: This explicitly uses Docker Compose's default network, allowing the service to communicate with other services if they're added later.
explanations.26: Each port mapping is defined in a structured way: the 'target' is the port inside the container, 'published' is what port it's exposed to on your machine, and 'mode: ingress' means it listens on all network interfaces.
explanations.34: This security setting prevents the container from gaining new privileges, which is a best practice to limit what processes inside could escalate to.
explanations.36: The container runs as user ID 1001 with group ID 1001, rather than as root, which is safer.
explanations.38: A 'bind' mount connects a folder on your computer directly to a folder inside the container so changes sync in real-time.
explanations.43: A 'volume' mount uses Docker's volume system (not a direct folder connection) to store data, which persists even if the container is deleted.
explanations.44: The VS Code extensions volume name — Docker will create and manage this storage area automatically so your VS Code extensions don't get lost.
explanations.54: This creates a custom name for the default network that all services in this compose file will use to communicate.
